reason: Compares texture (hardness, elasticity, chewiness, cohesiveness) of beef cooked by traditional boiling (control), sous vide, and sous vide with bromelain; there is no raw-beef reference in the table.
foods: beef (Longissimus thoracis muscles of Simmental cattle; pieces 4 × 4 × 5 cm3, 100 ± 5 g)
treatments: Control: traditional boiling for 120 min without bromelain or vacuum packaging; SV: sous vide cooking only (65 °C, 120 min; heating time counted from core temperature reaching set value, constant temperature water bath); SV + Bro: 10 mL bromelain solution (250 U/mL) injected per 100 ± 5 g meat, hand-massaged 1 min, vacuum sealed, incubated in water bath at 30 °C for 30 min, then SV 65 °C for 120 min, then ice-water bath
methods_quote: The group without bromelain, subjected only to SV cooking (65 °C, 120 min), was labeled as the SV group. The control group underwent traditional boiling for 120 min without bromelain or vacuum packaging.
units: Hardness (N); Elasticity (mm); Chewiness (N); Cohesiveness (no unit stated)
replicates: Measurements were conducted in parallel five times.
